gsplat-rust-renderer vs Brush

Pixel-level comparison, calibration, and interactive-viewer validation of our wgpu/WGSL Gaussian-splat renderer against the Brush reference implementation.

1. Executive summary — does our renderer match Brush?

Yes — after one root-cause fix, ours is pixel-identical to Brush for practical purposes. Phase 2 measured a global mean of 27.11 dB PSNR / 0.9486 SSIM across 24 matched test views (3 NeRF-synthetic scenes × 8 views), with one systematic difference: a feathered low-opacity silhouette halo past object boundaries, worst on ship (19.61 dB mean). Phase 3 (§5) ran pixel forensics, PLY population audits, a CPU re-implementation of the shader math, and a 3-experiment ablation, and proved the halo is a view-space covariance z-convention sign error in our projection stage: σxz/σyz entered the Jacobian with OpenGL sign while the surrounding math assumes a z-forward frame. Negating the z lane of the world-to-view rotation (shader/gaussian_project.wgsl + the Rust reference src/gsplat_core/covariance.rs) lifted ours-vs-Brush to 61.68 dB mean PSNR / 0.9995 SSIM / 0.0054 LPIPS (worst single view 56.74 dB — mean error well below 1/255), and ours-vs-GT now equals Brush-vs-GT (30.86 dB) to within 0.01 dB / 0.0002 SSIM on every individual view.

Geometry is verified independently of trained scenes: on the synthetic calibration scene both gsplat-render and Brush's render_ply place all 9 color-resolvable markers within ≤0.21 px of analytic projections (origin verified to 0.044 px / 0.040 px by manual cluster separation; the checker's origin "FAIL" is a blob-detection artifact of gray-on-white masking, §3), and the occluded depth-back marker is correctly invisible in both — depth ordering matches.

The interactive Rerun 0.33 viewer path also passes: 9/9 markers + handedness + occlusion on screenshots, measured effective FOV 55.216° (matches Rerun's default 55° eye), and at matched FOV the viewer screenshot reproduces the CLI render at SSIM 0.9981 (calibration) and 0.9946 (chair f0). 36/36 orbit screenshots non-blank with no popping; 3/3 saved .rrd files verify cleanly and reload with blueprint intact. (Viewer screenshots were captured before the phase-3 fix; the pose/FOV/occlusion conclusions are unaffected — the calibration markers are near-isotropic gaussians for which the σxz/σyz flip is negligible, ≤0.21 px agreement with analytic projections either way.)

Phase 4 (§9) then replaced the per-frame CPU frustum-cull + rayon depth-sort pre-pass — and its silent 200,000-splat cap — with Brush's GPU-only pipeline (GPU cull/compaction + GPU radix depth-argsort) in both render paths. Parity held on all 24 views (worst per-view delta −0.17 dB against a −0.3 dB gate; calibration bit-exact), throughput improved in all 6 benchmark cells (chair 800×800: 168.5 → 213.2 FPS), and a 309,888-splat cloud — 1.55× over the old cap, which would previously have silently dropped ~35% of the splats — now renders correctly.

Phase-2 anchor against ground truth (pre-fix): ours 25.05 dB vs Brush 30.86 dB mean PSNR to GT — the halo cost us background pixels. Post-fix the gap is gone (full before→after tables in §4).

2. Methodology

Three independent validation loops, each catching a different failure class:

Loop A — pixel-exact comparison vs Brush (offline CLIs)

Both renderers consume the same PLY and the same camera JSON and write 800×800 PNGs on a white background. Ours: gsplat-render (this package). Brush: a ~170-line harness crate render_ply added to Brush HEAD f043db46 that reuses Brush's own code end-to-end (brush_dataset::load_dataset, brush_serde::load_splat_from_ply, brush_render::render_splats) — every pixel comes from Brush code; no render-only CLI exists at HEAD. 3 scenes × 8 views; metrics: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS (AlexNet), plus amplified per-pixel diff maps (mean |Δ| ×8, viridis).

Loop B — ground-truth anchor

The same views are scored against NeRF-synthetic test images (RGBA composited onto white). This catches errors that a renderer-vs-renderer diff cannot (e.g. both being wrong the same way) and ranks each renderer's absolute reconstruction quality.

Loop C — interactive viewer (Rerun 0.33, native headless screenshots)

The full gRPC → Rerun-viewer → custom GaussianSplats3D visualizer path is exercised headlessly: ViewerClient.spawn(headless=True) against our viewer binary, per-pose Spatial3DView blueprints with EyeControls3D, view-specific save_screenshot crops. Screenshots are checked for marker geometry, orbit coverage/popping, matched-pose similarity vs the CLI renders, and .rrd save/reload round-trips.

Camera contract

All offline renders share the NeRF-synthetic camera convention: transforms_test.json gives camera_angle_x (fx = 0.5·w / tan(camera_angle_x/2), square pixels, centered principal point) and a 4×4 OpenGL-style camera-to-world per frame (+x right, +y up, camera looks along −z). Brush's nerfstudio reader applies its y/z-flip internally; our loader does the same conversion, so both CLIs receive identical pinhole intrinsics + extrinsics. The Rerun viewer cannot take a raw c2w matrix or FOV: poses are mapped to EyeControls3D(position=c2w[:3,3], look_target=position−4·c2w[:3,2], eye_up=c2w[:3,1]) and the viewer renders at its built-in vertical FOV (no FOV/zoom parameter at 0.33), so the effective FOV was measured from the calibration screenshot (55.216°) and matched-FOV crops/synthesized renders are used for comparisons.

How the calibration scene works

tools/calibration_scene.py generate builds a PLY of 10 tiny, near-isotropic, opacity≈1 gaussians at exactly known 3D points — origin (gray 0.85), axis tips +x (red) / +y (green) / +z (blue), four unit-square corners (yellow / cyan / magenta / gray 0.3), and a depth probe: an orange marker 0.05 in front of a purple one on the same camera ray, so the purple marker must be invisible if depth ordering is correct. It also writes a one-frame transforms_test.json and expected_pixels.json with the analytic pinhole projection of every marker. check renders the scene, detects each marker's color-blob centroid, and compares against the expected pixels (tolerance 2 px). Handedness, axis orientation, FOV, and depth ordering all become single-pixel assertions.

*Origin "FAIL" is a checker artifact, not geometry — identical in both renderers. The origin marker is gray (0.85, 0.85, 0.85) on a white background. At the default --color-tolerance 0.25 the color mask matches the entire white background (|1.0−0.85|=0.15<0.25), dragging the global centroid to image center (error 86.06 px = |486−400|). Tightening to 0.12 excludes the background, but the anti-aliased rim of the gray-0.3 corner-mm marker blends through exactly 0.85 against white and contaminates the mask (753 ring px vs 540 marker px → ~149 px). No tolerance value separates identical gray values with a global-mask centroid. Manual connected-component separation confirms the origin at (400.00, 486.00): 0.044 px (ours) / 0.040 px (Brush), and the contaminating ring cluster sits 0.058/0.056 px from corner-mm — independently confirming geometry. Tolerances were not relaxed; full writeup in /tmp/gsplat-compare/calibration/diagnosis.json. Verdict: both renderers' geometry verified — 9/9 color-resolvable markers ≤0.21 px, occluded marker correctly hidden.

Phase-2 worst-view diagnoses (ship) — historical, resolved by the §5 fix

  • ship f100 (15.87 dB, max abs diff 0.999) — Bright diff ring at the water-basin silhouette plus broad water-surface diff on this close-up view — ours bleeds a low-opacity gaussian halo past the silhouette onto the white background where Brush clips the splat extent crisply (8.5% of pixels diff > 0.1, concentrated in the bottom half at the basin rim).
  • ship f0 (19.68 dB) — Yellow ring around the entire dish silhouette in the diff map with a mostly-matching interior — the same silhouette halo bleed; our edge is feathered/smoky vs Brush's crisp boundary (7.9% of Brush's white-background pixels are non-white in ours).
  • ship f175 (19.74 dB) — Identical signature — feathered "fur" around the basin rim in ours vs a crisp edge in Brush, bright silhouette ring in the diff map; the interior water shows only low-level diff.

Phase-2 diagnosis across all three: a systematic gaussian footprint difference — ours rendered long low-opacity tails past the splat boundary where Brush cut off crisply, and the scene ranking chair > hotdog > ship tracked the population of large low-opacity splats. Phase 3 (§5) proved this "halo" was not an extent-cutoff difference at all but a covariance z-convention sign bug. After the fix these three views measure 59.15 / 57.35 / 57.63 dB ours-vs-Brush (f100 / f0 / f175).

Pixel-peeping — global worst view, full resolution, before → after

ship f100 at native 800×800 lossless PNG. Before the fix (15.87 dB ours-vs-brush) the basin rim grows feathered wedges and streaks onto the white background; after the fix (59.15 dB) ours is visually indistinguishable from Brush (max abs pixel diff 0.081).

5. Phase 3 — divergence hunt: forensics, ablation, root cause

Phase 2 left one open question: why does ours grow a feathered halo past silhouettes where Brush clips crisply? Phase 3 answered it in three steps — (a) pixel forensics + PLY population audit to classify the artifact, (b) a CPU re-implementation of the exact shader math to prove the candidate root cause offline, and (c) a controlled ablation in the renderer to confirm it and keep the fix.

5.1 Forensics — what the artifact actually is

Classification: (b)+(d) hybrid — large smooth gaussian wedges and directional streaks from REAL splats whose projected 2D covariance is wrong, NOT extra population. Evidence:

  1. NOT tile-aligned: fur-mask tile-grid occupancy 0.123–0.128 vs random 0.125 (ship f100/f0) — rules out tile/binning bugs.
  2. NOT many small blobs: ship f100 fur mask 47,869 px in 423 connected components but ONE CC holds 42,491 px (89%); f0: 19,073 of 32,281 px in the top CC — few giant structures, not a population of stray splats.
  3. NOT faint: the background luminance-deficit histogram is heavy-tailed (f100: 14,084 px in [128,256), mean deficit of >1px = 64.3) — near-opaque coverage where Brush is pure white, so it cannot be a sub-1/255-cutoff tail difference.
  4. Geometry signature: streak orientation rotates with camera azimuth (horizontal at f100, diagonal arcs at f0) and severity grows toward the image periphery (regions found at y=518–650, x=26/236/387/650) — exactly the signature of a σxz/σyz cross-term sign error whose magnitude scales with (f/z)²·|u,v|·|σxz|.

Root cause proven by CPU simulation: re-implementing the exact shader math in numpy, the buggy convention (raw OpenGL view-space covariance fed to a z-forward Jacobian) reproduces our render's background coverage at r = 0.9951 (mean coverage 0.0426 vs render 0.0400); negating the covariance z row/col (correct z-forward convention) yields background coverage 0.0009, matching Brush's 0.0008. Bug location: shader/gaussian_project.wgsl lines 474–502 set camera_depth = -mean_view.z and mean_camera = (x, y, depth) (z-forward) but lines 490–494 built view_linear from the raw OpenGL view_from_world and line 233 computes covariance_view = view_linear·cov·view_linearᵀ without negating the z row — so σxz/σyz kept OpenGL sign while the Jacobian (lines 204–221) assumes z-forward. Same bug in the Rust reference src/gsplat_core/covariance.rs:50-51. Scene scaling matches: error ∝ view-space tilt covariance σxz/σyz, largest for ship's grazing-angle water needles (anisotropy p99 226,028), smallest for chair's fluffier splats.

Zoomed forensic crops below: highest-energy background-adjacent |ours−Brush| regions, 150×150-px crops upscaled 6× nearest. Panels left→right: GT | ours (baseline) | Brush | |ours−Brush|×8.

Audit conclusion: ALL quats are exactly unit-norm (Brush's export normalizes at write, export.rs:156-167) — the degenerate-quat culling difference between our loader (normalize_quat_or_identity keeps them) and Brush (project_forward culls qnorm²<1e-6) is a no-op for these scenes. No giant floaters (max world scale 0.445), no NaNs, no off-bbox population. The only cross-scene gradient matching artifact severity (chair < hotdog < ship) is extreme-anisotropy needle count combined with grazing view geometry — consistent with the covariance cross-term sign bug, not with any population difference.

What each attempt rendered — ship f100

5.3 Root cause & the kept fix

Root cause: view-space covariance z-convention sign error in the projection stage. shader/gaussian_project.wgsl project_main built view_linear from the raw OpenGL-style view_from_world rotation (camera looks down −z), but mean_camera = (view.x, view.y, −view.z) and the brush-style Jacobian (brush_camera_jacobian_rows) assume a z-forward frame. The frame change is diag(1, 1, −1), so σxz/σyz entered J·Σ·Jᵀ with flipped sign, producing wrong 2D shear that grows with (f/z)²·|u,v|·|σxz| — the peripheral wedges/streaks and feathered halos, worst on ship's extreme-anisotropy water needles (anisotropy p99 226k), least on chair. Same bug mirrored in the Rust reference src/gsplat_core/covariance.rs. Fix: negate the z row of the world-to-view rotation before forming Σview (only σxz/σyz flip; xx/xy/yy/zz unchanged). The one-line-class fix took ours-vs-Brush from 15.87 to 59.15 dB on the worst view and made ours-vs-GT equal Brush-vs-GT to 0.01 dB on all 24 views.

Changes kept in the working tree:

  • shader/gaussian_project.wgsl (project_main, formerly lines 490–494): view_linear now built from view_from_world columns with negated z lane — vc0/vc1/vc2 = view_from_world[0..2].xyz; view_linear = mat3x3f(vec3f(vc0.x, vc0.y, -vc0.z), vec3f(vc1.x, vc1.y, -vc1.z), vec3f(vc2.x, vc2.y, -vc2.z)) — plus a 5-line comment explaining the z-forward frame convention.
  • src/gsplat_core/covariance.rs (brush_covariance_in_pixels, formerly lines 50–51): view_linear_gl = mat3_from_affine(camera.view_from_world); view_linear = Mat3::from_cols with the .z component of each column negated (mirrors the shader; reference impl only, no render-path callers).
  • No other files changed: constants.rs, culling.rs, ply_loader.rs verified byte-identical to pre-ablation backups; the uncommitted 0.33-upgrade changes (Cargo.toml/lock, main.rs, gaussian_renderer.rs, gaussian_visualizer.rs, pixi.*) are untouched.

Post-fix verification: full 24-view matrix re-rendered and re-scored → /tmp/gsplat-compare-fixed/metrics.json. Fixed ours-vs-GT PSNR/SSIM equals brush-vs-GT to within 0.01 dB / 0.0002 SSIM on every individual view (worst per-view ours-vs-brush: ship f25 56.74 dB; best: chair f0 67.20 dB; max abs pixel diff ≤ 0.098). All before→after tables in §4 use these numbers.

6. Viewer validation (Rerun 0.33, native headless)

Verdict: PASS. 45/45 headless screenshots captured with zero failures; 9/9 calibration markers + occlusion + handedness on screenshots; FOV fit RMS 2.71 px; matched-FOV SSIM 0.9981 (calibration) / 0.9946 (chair f0) vs the CLI renderer; 36/36 orbit shots non-blank with no popping flagged; 3/3 .rrd files verified; blueprint reload round-trip OK.

Capture method. ViewerClient.spawn(headless=True, port=9879, executable_path=<our 0.33 viewer binary>, hide_welcome_screen=True) from the worktree pixi env (rerun-sdk 0.33.0). One viewer process per scene; a fresh Spatial3DView blueprint per camera pose (the eye snaps to EyeControls3D position/look_target/eye_up); 2.5 s settle per blueprint; view-specific save_screenshot(view_id=...) yields chrome-free 1593×810 crops of the 1600×900 window. The X11 fallback was never needed. 7. Brush evolution & adoption recommendations

Since v0.3.0 (3edecbb2, 2025-09-14 — our cloning baseline) Brush has landed 169 commits to HEAD f043db46 (2026-06-06). The biggest structural change is #411: all WGSL shaders were ported to Rust CubeCL kernels. Commit d0eaca6f — the parent of that port — is the last full-WGSL snapshot and already contains the #386 subgroup sort and #394 raster speedups; it is our designated WGSL porting source. Core algorithm and constants are unchanged from what we cloned (16×16 tiles, Morton order, StopThePop intersection, blur 0.3, alpha cutoff 1/255, Sloan SH); our CPU pre-sort with the 200k cap is our own deviation, and Brush shows exactly how to replace it — done in Phase 4 (§9).

Ranked adoption list

  1. Replace the CPU frustum-cull + depth sort with Brush's GPU pipeline: atomic compaction of (id, depth) in the project kernel + 32-bit radix argsort over f32 depth bits, using v0.3.0-style indirect dispatch to stay GPU-only. Removes the 200k-splat cap and is the only item that changes output quality on large scenes. (refs: render.rs DepthSort, project_forward.rs)
  2. Port the #386 subgroup radix sort by lifting the WGSL verbatim from commit d0eaca6f (crates/brush-sort/src/shaders/*.wgsl): ~50% faster sorting, 10-15% faster frames; includes the #385 chunked-scan corruption fix needed once the splat cap is gone. Requires wgpu Features::SUBGROUP + 'enable subgroups;'.
  3. Apply the #394 rasterizer diff (commit d658a6d9): workgroup-shared num_done_atomic cooperative early-exit, gated compact_gid loads, deferred rgb reads. ~20 lines of WGSL, pure win on dense scenes.
  4. Harden the intersection pipeline like #411/#373/#459: share one will_primitive_contribute loop body between count and write passes, write at most min(counted, budgeted) entries, pad leftover slots with sentinel tile_id = num_tiles, and gate tile_offsets writes on tid < num_tiles.
  5. Add the optional Mip-Splatting render mode (#337): cov_blur 0.1 + opacity *= sqrt(det_raw/det_blurred), selected per-PLY; default path stays exactly our current 0.3-blur behavior. Needed to render mip-trained PLYs correctly.
  6. Adopt the cheap numerical guards from HEAD: 1e18 PSD-preserving covariance clamp, degenerate-conic extent sentinel, SH color NaN-scrub + [-100,100] clamp, positively-phrased finite checks.
  7. Audit every dispatch site for the 65535-workgroup limit (4K = exactly 65536 tiles) — we have dispatch_grid_for_workgroups but must verify shader-side 2D index recovery everywhere.
  8. Add Brush-style invariance tests (hidden/culled splats don't perturb output, determinism, NaN loud-failure) and a sort regression test; lift scenarios from crates/brush-render/src/tests/mod.rs.
  9. Do NOT port: the CubeCL kernel framework (we stay raw WGSL; use d0eaca6f as the WGSL porting source), the synchronous count readback (conflicts with GPU-only constraint; keep capacity+GPU-clamp), training-only changes (smooth alpha cutoff #448, backward kernels, fused losses #394/#401/#410, densification #265/#390/#479).
  10. Defer unless needed: fisheye camera models (KB4/RT8/ThinPrism #434/#447 — large effort, only for non-pinhole data; do take the CPU-precomputed Jacobian clamp limits), LOD-baked _lodN.ply awareness, brush-js-style zero-copy embedding.

Do-not-port list

  • CubeCL kernel framework (#411) — we intentionally stay raw WGSL; treat HEAD kernels/*.rs as readable spec only and lift WGSL from d0eaca6f.
  • Synchronous exact-count CPU readback (#350/#340) — stalls the pipeline and conflicts with our GPU-only constraint; keep capacity buffers + GPU clamp (mirrors Brush v0.3.0's indirect-dispatch design). Optionally add an async frame-delayed readback purely to grow capacity.
  • Training-only changes — smooth alpha cutoff (#448), backward kernels, fused losses (#394/#401/#410), densification (#265/#390/#479): we render, we don't train.
  • Defer unless needed — fisheye camera models KB4/RT8/ThinPrism (#434/#447; do take the CPU-precomputed Jacobian clamp limits), LOD-baked _lodN.ply awareness, brush-js zero-copy embedding.

9. Phase 4 — GPU-only pipeline & throughput

With pixel parity proven (§4–5), phase 4 removed our one remaining architectural deviation from Brush: the per-frame CPU pre-pass (frustum cull → hard cap at 200,000 splats → rayon back-to-front depth sort in rebuild_visible_indices(), src/gsplat_core/culling.rs) that fed sorted indices to the GPU. Both render paths — the standalone CLI (src/gsplat_core/gpu_renderer.rs) and the Rerun viewer visualizer (src/gaussian_renderer.rs) — now run Brush's fully-GPU pipeline: GPU visibility culling with atomic stream compaction, then a GPU radix depth argsort, with zero per-splat CPU work per frame (remaining CPU duties: uniform writes + command encoding). The 200k cap is gone. Design doc: /tmp/port-design.md.

9.1 Architecture — before → after

BEFORE — CPU pre-pass per frame

PLY → splat buffers
↓
CPU, every frame: frustum cull → cap at 200,000 splats → rayon back-to-front depth sort rebuild_visible_indices() · src/gsplat_core/culling.rs — DELETED
↓
upload sorted index buffer (per-frame write_buffer) CachedComputeResources::index_buffer + cpu_indices — DELETED
↓
GPU project_main — one thread per pre-sorted visible splat gaussian_project.wgsl
↓
tile-hit prefix sum — 2-level, silently capped at 512×512 = 262,144 elements
↓
map intersections → 4-bit radix sort by tile id gaussian_dynamic_sort.wgsl
↓
tile offsets → 16×16 tile raster → composite (viewer) / readback (CLI)

AFTER — GPU-only (Brush port)

PLY → splat buffers (no per-frame index upload)
↓
GPU project_forward_main — one thread per splat over the FULL cloud; every visibility gate; survivors compacted via atomicAdd(num_visible) → global_from_compact[] + depth_keys[] gaussian_project.wgsl — shares project_splat() with project_visible_main
↓
GPU depth argsort — gid-canonicalization passes, then 8×4-bit radix passes ascending over f32 depth bits ⇒ compact order is front-to-back; key count read from the num_visible GPU buffer (no readback, no indirect dispatch) gaussian_dynamic_sort.wgsl · brush v0.3.0 capacity-dispatch pattern
↓
GPU project_visible_main — reads gid via sorted global_from_compact, recomputes projection + SH, writes at compact_id; zero-fills tail [num_visible, capacity)
↓

↓

↓

9.2 What was ported, exactly

  1. Two projection entry points, one shared project_splat() helper (gaussian_project.wgsl) so cull and shade math agree bit-for-bit. project_forward_main is capacity-dispatched on cloud.len() and applies every visibility gate: near-plane depth in the z-forward frame (keeping the §5 covariance z-sign fix), opacity ≥ 1/255, finite meanpx/power_threshold/extent, radius ≥ MIN_RADIUS_PX, and Brush's extent-aware mean±extent-vs-viewport on-screen test (replacing the old CPU |NDC|>1.5 center cull). Survivors: write_id = atomicAdd(num_visible); global_from_compact[write_id] = gid; depth_keys[write_id] = bitcast<u32>(depth).
  2. Depth argsort reuses the existing tile-sort machinery (gaussian_dynamic_sort.wgsl): key count read from the num_visible GPU buffer, capacity-dispatched with shader early-exit — the brush v0.3.0 pattern, no CPU readback and no indirect dispatch. 8 ascending passes over f32 depth bits make the compact order front-to-back directly; the old CPU reverse-upload is gone.
  3. Determinism beyond brush — gid canonicalization. Brush's atomicAdd compaction leaves the order of equal depth keys nondeterministic; we observed ~30 coincidental f32 depth-bit collisions in chair causing run-to-run pixel flips and a −0.86 dB parity miss on chair f175. A preceding gid-sort stage (gid_sort_passes(), even pass count) sorts the (gid, depth) pairs by gid first, so the stable depth sort resolves ties ascending-gid — verified bit-identical renders across runs.
  4. project_visible_main (the restructured project_main) is capacity-dispatched on cloud.len(), early-exits for compact_id ≥ num_visible while zeroing the ProjectedTileSplat + tile_hit_count slots in [num_visible, capacity) so the capacity-sized scan sees zeros; per the brush model PF is the sole gate — PV never culls. It re-projects, evaluates SH, and writes outputs at compact_id.
  5. 3-level prefix scan. The old 2-level tile-hit scan silently capped at 512 blocks × 512 = 262,144 elements — exactly the old 200k-cap envelope. A third level reuses existing entry points (scan_blocks on level-1 block sums + scan_block_sums + sort_scan_compose_main recombination); clouds up to ~134M splats now scan correctly. Scan/map uniforms stay CPU-set to capacity values with zeroed tails (the documented simpler-correct option; no count binding added to the scan).
  6. Deleted: src/gsplat_core/culling.rs (rebuild_visible_indices + build_compute_candidate), SortedSplatIndex, MAX_SPLATS_RENDERED, PARALLEL_SPLAT_THRESHOLD, the rayon dependency, the per-frame index-buffer upload + cpu_indices, the dead InstanceData/visibility_flags/scatter_main instanced path, dummy_instance_buf, and the descending-depth-key helper. Proof: grep -rn "rebuild_visible_indices|par_sort|select_nth_unstable|rayon" src/ shader/ → zero hits; rayon removed from Cargo.toml (it remains in the lockfile only as a transitive dep of the re_* viewer crates).
  7. Single source of truth for both render paths: project_forward/project_visible bind-group layouts + pipelines, DEPTH_SORT_PASSES, gid_sort_passes, and a deduplicated encode_radix_sort helper (used by both the depth and tile sorts) live in src/gsplat_core/gpu_types.rs; viewer (gaussian_renderer.rs, persistent buffers) and CLI (gpu_renderer.rs, per-call allocation) share them. API surface: add_batch(ctx, label, cloud, camera) only.

Documented deviations from brush: (a) near-plane cull uses camera.near_plane — our existing GPU gate — instead of brush's fixed 0.01; (b) the gid-canonicalization sort for determinism (brush ships the nondeterminism); (c) the InstanceData-only NDC culls were dropped from the gate — provably implied by the kept culls, confirmed by parity.

After-port is faster in all 6 cells. The remaining 2.1–3.2× gap vs Brush is dominated by the CLI harness itself: every timed gpu_render() call allocates all GPU buffers, re-uploads the splats, and ends with a blocking full-frame RGBA8 readback (map_async + poll-to-completion), so frames cannot pipeline — the viewer path reuses persistent buffers. Timing includes that allocation + upload + readback; pipeline JIT is excluded by the warmup frame.

9.5 Past the old 200k cap — 309,888 splats, and the raster micro-port

To prove the cap is gone end-to-end, ship.ply (19,368 splats) was tiled 16× with uniform ±0.02 xyz jitter (numpy seed 42, plyfile) → /tmp/gsplat-port/ship_x16.ply, 309,888 splats = 1.55× the old 200,000 cap. The new binary renders frame 0 at 800×800 with no panic (exit 0), reports "309888 splats", and benchmarks at 31.9 ms / 31.3 FPS (20 frames, two runs within 0.1 ms; GPU memory steady at 1504 MiB). The old binary's CPU pre-pass hard-capped visible indices at 200,000 and would have silently dropped 109,888 splats (~35% of the cloud), rendering an incorrect truncated image. The headless viewer renders the same cloud (persistent-buffer gaussian_renderer.rs path): screenshot std 45.6, coverage 13.6%, all 16 jittered copies visible.

Raster micro-port (kept, bit-identical): two changes from Brush's newer raster work were applied to gaussian_raster_tiles.wgsl. (1) #394 early tile exit — var<workgroup> num_done: atomic<u32> + a plain num_done_uniform mirror: outside pixels add 1 up front, each pixel adds 1 once on saturation (T ≤ 1e-4), and the whole workgroup breaks the batch loop when workgroupUniformLoad(num_done_uniform) == TILE_SIZE (the uniform-load's internal barriers replace the old leading workgroupBarrier). (2) Deferred color read (from brush-research rasterize.rs) — sigma/alpha computed from xy_px + conic_xyy_opacity (opacity from conic.w, bit-equal to color_rgba.a); color_rgba.rgb is read only in the contributing branch; blending math unchanged. Parity: all 24 views + calibration bit-identical (max abs diff 0) before vs after; benchmark moved 4.1 → 4.0 ms on ship f0 (within run jitter — the CLI path is allocation-dominated).

10. Phase 5 — performance: closing (and passing) the Brush gap

Goal gates: ≥90% of Brush throughput per cell, ≥98% of Brush accuracy on all 24 views, viewer intact, ~10% LOC reduction. Worktree committed in 4 slices first (z-sign fix / 0.33+headless / GPU-only port / calibration+docs) so each perf change diffs cleanly.

10.1 E5 — persistent GPU resources + RGBA8 readback (standalone CLI)

Phase-4 profiling showed the biggest cost in the standalone path was the harness, not the pipeline: gpu_render() re-created ~30 buffers and 11 bind groups, re-uploaded ~12.8 MB of splat data per call, then round-tripped every pixel u8→f32→u8 through a 10 MB Vec. E5 moves all of it into a persistent GpuRenderResources built once per (cloud, resolution): splat upload, scratch buffers, radix-sort pass bind groups (prebuilt per shift × src/dst parity, shift uniforms shared by all three sorts), raster texture and the mappable staging buffer. Per frame the CPU writes one ~450-byte camera uniform, encodes the (unchanged) dispatch sequence, and reads back raw RGBA8 rows with the padding stripped — no per-pixel conversion. Each radix sort also now encodes all its passes inside a single compute pass (dispatch order identical; WebGPU guarantees dispatch-order visibility within a pass).

This also makes the benchmark apples-to-apples with Brush, whose harness reuses resources across iterations the same way. --benchmark --output saves the last benchmark frame as a standing buffer-reuse proof: frame 50 must (and does) equal a single-shot render byte-for-byte.

10.2 R1+R2+E1 — one render path, no per-frame object churn in the viewer

The viewer and the standalone CLI used to define the same 13 bind-group layouts, 14 compute pipelines, radix-sort encoder, and 9 pipeline bind-group wirings twice. Now gpu_types.rs is the single source of truth: RadixSort (prebuilt per-pass bind groups; all passes of one sort encoded into a single compute pass) and create_pipeline_bind_groups are shared by both paths. The viewer's per-frame encode_radix_sort — which created ~19 uniform buffers, ~110 bind groups, and ~110 label Strings every frame across the gid/depth/tile sorts — is gone; three prebuilt RadixSorts live in the per-entity cache and are rebuilt only when buffers grow or the raster extent changes. gaussian_renderer.rs shrank 2,556 → 1,565 lines; Rust+WGSL total 8,422 → 7,524 (pre-phase-5 baseline 8,264).

Gates: all 24 views, the calibration scene, and the 310k cloud stay bit-identical; CLI bench equal or better (1600² cells improved ~3–7%, e.g. chair 2.208 → 2.108 ms — fewer compute-pass boundaries); full viewer validation pass — matched-pose best-aligned SSIM vs CLI 0.9922 (identical to the pre-change value), new-vs-old screenshot SSIM 1.0000, rrd verify clean, save→reload→screenshot PASS, 309,888-splat viewer render PASS (report: /tmp/rerun-viewer-validation/20260610-gsplat-r1e1/).

10.3 Deliberately not ported: subgroup sort (#386), scan compaction (E3), indirect dispatch (E4)

These were ranked as the path to close a 2.2× gap; after E5 + R1/R2/E1 ours is faster than Brush in all six cells, so they would now trade away bit-identical renders (subgroup ops reorder float operations) or add kernels/LOC for speed the gates don't need. Kept as future work in §7's adoption list — relevant again only if a much heavier workload (multi-million splats, 4K) reopens the gap.

10.5 Scale check — Tanks & Temples train (1.07M splats) vs Brush vs GT

Same three-way comparison as the NeRF-synthetic scenes, on a 27× larger real-world scene: the official INRIA-trained 30k-iteration train PLY (1,071,462 splats, camenduru/gaussian-splatting) evaluated against the tandt_db GT images on the standard 3DGS protocol (every 8th image, 8 views, 980×545). COLMAP poses converted once to a staged NeRF-style dataset consumed by both renderers (principal point is exactly centered; the 0.4% fx/fy anisotropy is approximated identically for both, so the parity comparison is exact).

The two views under the informal 50 dB watch threshold (r_0, r_2) were examined: the difference is a distributed sub-2/255 imprint over the whole image (only 0.03% of pixels exceed 2/255, no localized structure) — float-accumulation ordering under deep overdraw, the expected scaling of the same sub-LSB noise that measures 56–67 dB on 40k-splat scenes.

11. Appendix — reproduction commands

# Paths
# PKG = packages/gsplat-rust-renderer (worktree .claude/worktrees/feature-splatting)
# ENVBIN = <worktree>/.pixi/envs/gsplat-rust-renderer/bin  (python w/ rerun-sdk 0.33, rerun CLI)

# 0. Build ours (CLI + viewer binary)
cd $PKG && cargo build --release            # -> target/release/gsplat-render
cargo build --release --features viewer      # -> target/release/gsplat-rust-renderer

# 1. Build the Brush reference harness (Brush HEAD f043db46 + render-ply crate)
cd /tmp/brush && cargo build --release -p render-ply   # -> target/release/render_ply

# 2. Offline matrix: 3 scenes x 8 views x {ours, brush}, 800x800 white bg
for S in chair hotdog ship; do for F in 0 25 50 75 100 125 150 175; do
  $PKG/target/release/gsplat-render --ply $PKG/data/trained/$S.ply \
    --camera $PKG/data/nerf-synthetic/$S/transforms_test.json --frame $F \
    --width 800 --height 800 --background 1,1,1 --output /tmp/gsplat-compare/$S/ours_f$F.png
  /tmp/brush/target/release/render_ply --ply $PKG/data/trained/$S.ply \
    --dataset $PKG/data/nerf-synthetic/$S --frame $F \
    --width 800 --height 800 --background 1,1,1 --out /tmp/gsplat-compare/$S/brush_f$F.png
done; done

# 3. Metrics (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS + diff maps) -> /tmp/gsplat-compare/metrics.json
$ENVBIN/python /tmp/gsplat-compare/run_metrics.py

# 4. Calibration scene: generate, render with both, check
$ENVBIN/python $PKG/tools/calibration_scene.py generate --out-dir $PKG/data/calibration
$PKG/target/release/gsplat-render --ply $PKG/data/calibration/calibration.ply \
  --camera $PKG/data/calibration/transforms_test.json --frame 0 \
  --background 1,1,1 --output /tmp/gsplat-compare/calibration/gsplat-render.png
/tmp/brush/target/release/render_ply --ply $PKG/data/calibration/calibration.ply \
  --dataset $PKG/data/calibration --frame 0 --width 800 --height 800 \
  --background 1,1,1 --out /tmp/gsplat-compare/calibration/brush.png
$ENVBIN/python $PKG/tools/calibration_scene.py check \
  --image /tmp/gsplat-compare/calibration/gsplat-render.png \
  --expected $PKG/data/calibration/expected_pixels.json \
  --report /tmp/gsplat-compare/calibration/gsplat-render.json
# origin gray-on-white artifact: see /tmp/gsplat-compare/calibration/diagnosis.json

# 5. Viewer validation (Rerun 0.33, native headless) — R = /tmp/rerun-viewer-validation/20260610-gsplat-brush-033
$ENVBIN/python $R/make_poses.py
$ENVBIN/python $R/capture.py --scene calibration --ply $PKG/data/calibration/calibration.ply \
  --poses $R/poses/calibration.json --out-dir $R/screenshots --bg black --full-shot-for calibration_pose
$ENVBIN/python $R/fit_calibration.py        # marker detection + FOV fit -> calibration_fit.json
$ENVBIN/python $R/matched_fov_check.py      # synthesized-FOV CLI render cross-check
$ENVBIN/python $R/capture.py --scene chair --ply $PKG/data/trained/chair.ply \

$ENVBIN/python $R/analyze_scenes.py         # orbit/matched-pose analysis -> scene_analysis.json
$ENVBIN/rerun rrd verify $R/chair.rrd && $ENVBIN/rerun rrd stats $R/chair.rrd
$ENVBIN/python $R/reload_check.py           # .rrd blueprint reload round-trip

# 6. Headless smoke test (0.33 upgrade proof)
